answer: Each agent can earn only one scarce, nontransferable membership credential by completing a costly, randomly assigned task that is checked against a public record and expires unless renewed. The registry rejects duplicate credentials, so making many accounts does not multiply voting or payouts. An attacker must obtain and maintain a separate credential for every identity, paying the task cost repeatedly; spreading claims across comet, oasis, and tundra regions does not bypass the same check.
